prior_importants.description: MergeLockLostError is an Error subclass declared inline in merge-gate.service.ts, next to withMergeLock which throws it, instead of in merge-gate.errors.ts beside MergeLockHeldError (general.md §Code layout: no inline error classes).

findings.description: The new lost-lock check trusts a dev/ino match, but inode numbers get reused. If a session runs `rm -rf .git/pup-merge.lock` while gate A holds it, a waiting run B can make a fresh lock that reuses A's inode number (common on ext4). A's release then moves B's lock aside, sees a match and reports no MergeLockLostError, so two gates ran together and both look clean. ADR 0088's owed rename-back item (L151-154) has the same root cause and the same fix, a holder token in the lock; it should also name inode reuse after a remove-and-remake.

Two adjacent comments around the steer ("Right after the event, still under the lock…" and "Said now, before the audit…") both say the audit can throw and a re-run refuses. The steerOverlappingSessions and landSession JSDoc already say this. Keep one short WHY and delete the other (AGENTS.md §Comments: delete the call-site copy).

The comment above `const target = sanitizeReason(outcome.target)` ("Each peer the land could not steer was named on stderr…") describes what landSession does, not the code below it, and repeats land.service.ts's JSDoc and comments. Delete it (AGENTS.md §Comments: delete the call-site copy).

The type parameter on `MergeLockLostError<TResult = unknown>` buys no type safety. A catch clause cannot infer it, and both CLI catch sites still cast (`error.result as MergeOutcome` / `as LandOutcome`). `readonly result: unknown` removes the generic and keeps the casts unchanged.

Rename the boolean `fault` in removeLockDir to `isDiskFault`. general.md §Type safety requires boolean names to start with is/has/should/can, and `return fault` leaves the reader to work out that it means "count the lock as released".
Rename the boolean `asRoot` to `isRoot`. general.md §Type safety requires boolean names to start with is/has/should/can.
